root.label: Copy and move semantics
root.note: Move semantics transfers ownership from expiring objects while respecting constness and exception safety.

children.label: std::move and constness
children.note: std::move only casts to an rvalue reference and yields to copy semantics on const objects.

children.label: Unconditional rvalue cast
children.note: std::move produces an xvalue at compile time without emitting runtime instructions.

children.label: const T&& fallback
children.note: Applying std::move to a const variable creates const T&&, which calls the copy constructor.

children.label: Special member generation
children.note: User-declared destructors, copies, or moves alter which special members the compiler generates.

children.label: Destructor suppresses move
children.note: Declaring any destructor disables implicit move generation and falls back to copying.

children.label: Move deletes copy
children.note: Declaring a custom move operation implicitly deletes copy construction and copy assignment.

children.label: Rule of Zero vs Five
children.note: Compose RAII wrappers to avoid custom members, or explicitly define all five for raw handles.

children.label: Safe move implementation
children.note: Custom move operations must clear the source, survive self-assignment, and preserve invariants.

children.label: std::exchange
children.note: Atomically steals a pointer or handle value while resetting the source member to null.

children.label: Self-move guard
children.note: Checking this == &other prevents freeing your own buffer during a = std::move(a).

children.label: Valid unspecified state
children.note: Moved-from standard objects remain destructible and assignable without guaranteeing emptiness.

children.label: noexcept and containers
children.note: Containers use std::move_if_noexcept to preserve strong exception safety during reallocation.

children.label: std::move_if_noexcept
children.note: Selects rvalue move only if the move constructor is noexcept or copying is unavailable.

children.label: Explicit noexcept required
children.note: User-written move operations do not infer noexcept automatically and must annotate it.

children.label: Implicit move on return
children.note: Returning a local variable or parameter automatically attempts rvalue overload resolution first.

children.label: C++23 P2266R3 rules
children.note: Simpler implicit move treats move-eligible id-expressions uniformly as rvalues across conversions.
